```{r}
head(data)
str(data)
dim(data)
names(data)
summary(data)

colSums(is.na(data))

# Check duplicate participant IDs
sum(duplicated(data$ID))
```

```{r}
# Check whether values fall within the ranges
# specified in the assignment

summary(data$GradeStats)
summary(data$Judgment)
summary(data$Comprehension)

# Check categorical variables
table(data$Sexe, useNA = "ifany")
table(data$GoalStudy, useNA = "ifany")
```

### 2. Descriptive Statistics
```{r}
data %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_stats_courses = mean(StatsCourses, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_stats_courses = sd(StatsCourses, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_judgment = mean(Judgment, na.rm = TRUE),
```

### 3. Prepare the analysis dataset
```{r}
# do not automatically remove participants based on
# comprehension or guessed study purpose
# First inspect missingness and justify any exclusions.

analysis_data <- data %>%
  select(ID, StatsCourses, Judgment, Comprehension) %>%
  drop_na()

nrow(analysis_data)
```

### 4. RQ1
```{r}
# Association between statistics credits
# and the number of correct judgements

model_rq1 <- lm(
  Judgment ~ StatsCourses,
  data = analysis_data
)

summary(model_rq1)
confint(model_rq1)

# Check basic linear-model diagnostics
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model_rq1)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

### 5. RQ2
```{r}
# Does comprehension moderate the association?
# Center the continuous predictors to aid interpretation

analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(
    StatsCourses_c = StatsCourses - mean(StatsCourses),
    Comprehension_c = Comprehension - mean(Comprehension)
  )

model_rq2 <- lm(
  Judgment ~ StatsCourses_c * Comprehension_c,
  data = analysis_data
)

summary(model_rq2)
confint(model_rq2)

# Inspect the interaction visually
ggplot(
  analysis_data,
  aes(
    x = StatsCourses,
    y = Judgment,
    color = factor(
      if_else(Comprehension >= median(Comprehension),
              "Higher comprehension", "Lower comprehension")
    )
  )
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x = "Statistics course credits (ECs)",
    y = "Correct judgements",
    color = "Comprehension group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# 8. Extract model estimates for reporting

tidy(model_rq1, conf.int = TRUE)
tidy(model_rq2, conf.int = TRUE)

glance(model_rq1)
glance(model_rq2)
```

## Part 2: Check Computational Reproducitibility
### 1. Inspect the dataset
```{r}
# Check how many participants are in each category
table(data$GoalStudy)

# Check statistics grades
summary(data$GradeStats)
```

### 2. Prepare the dataset, one with 5.5 as the passing-grade threshold,
### another one with 6.0
```{r}
# Remove participants who guessed the study goal
# and participants with a non-passing statistics grade

clean_data_1 <- data %>%
  filter(GoalStudy == 0,
         GradeStats >= 5.5)

# Check remaining sample size
nrow(clean_data_1)

# Check the cleaned dataset
summary(clean_data_1)
```

```{r}
# Try 6.0 as the passing grade
clean_data_2 <- data %>%
  filter(GoalStudy == 0,
         GradeStats >= 6.0)

# Check remaining sample size
nrow(clean_data_2)

# Check the cleaned dataset
summary(clean_data_2)
```

```{r}
# Check how many people is removed
nrow(data) - nrow(clean_data_1)
nrow(data) - nrow(clean_data_2)
```

## 5. rq2
```{r}
# Mean-centering
clean_data_1 <- clean_data_1 %>%

    Comprehension_c = Comprehension - mean(Comprehension, na.rm = TRUE)

  )
```

```{r}
# Model 2.1: Moderation analysis with 5.5 as passing grade

model2_1 <- lm(Judgment ~ StatsCourses_c * Comprehension_c +
               ReadNews,
             data = clean_data_1)

# View results

```

```{r}

model2_2 <- lm(Judgment ~ StatsCourses_c * Comprehension_c +
               ReadNews,
             data = clean_data_2)

# View results
summary(model2_2)
```

## Part D: Conducting the Multiverse Analysis
### 1. Define the decisions and their options
```{r}
# Each decision in the multiverse is one argument of the pipeline.
# The options for each decision are listed here:
#
# D2 Grade:          keep all / exclude below 5.5 / exclude below 6.0
# D3 Comprehension:  keep all / exclude <= 7 (chance) / exclude <= 10 (not significantly above chance) / keep all, but add Comprehension as a predictor
# D5 Controls:       none / ReadNews / ReadNews + Age + Sexe

multiverse_options <- expand_grid(
  grade         = c("keep", "5.5", "6.0"),
  comprehension = c("keep", "exclude_7", "exclude_10", "covariate"),
  controls      = c("none", "readnews", "demographic")
)

# Number of pathways: 3 x 4 x 3 = 36
nrow(multiverse_options)
```

### 2. Data-processing functions
```{r}
# D2: remove participants whose average statistics grade is below the passing threshold
filter_grade <- function(df, grade) {
  if (grade == "keep") return(df)
  df %>% filter(GradeStats >= as.numeric(grade))
}

# D3: attention check. "Covariate" added in D5
filter_comprehension <- function(df, comprehension) {
  if (comprehension == "exclude_7")  return(df %>% filter(Comprehension > 7))
  if (comprehension == "exclude_10") return(df %>% filter(Comprehension > 10))
  df
}

```

### 3. Analysis functions
```{r}
# D3 + D5: build the regression formula. 
build_formula <- function(comprehension, controls) {
  predictors <- "StatsCourses"
  if (controls == "readnews")    predictors <- c(predictors, "ReadNews")
  if (controls == "demographic") predictors <- c(predictors, "ReadNews", "Age", "Sexe")
  if (comprehension == "covariate") predictors <- c(predictors, "Comprehension")
  as.formula(paste("Judgment ~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + ")))
}

# Run one complete pathway: apply the data-processing steps in a fixed order (D2 -> D3)
run_pathway <- function(grade, comprehension, controls) {
  df <- data %>%
    filter_grade(grade) %>%
    filter_comprehension(comprehension)

  model <- lm(build_formula(comprehension, controls), data = df)
  est   <- tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE) %>% filter(term == "StatsCourses")

  tibble(
    n         = nrow(df),
    estimate  = est$estimate,
    conf.low  = est$conf.low,
    conf.high = est$conf.high,
    t         = est$statistic,
    p_one     = pt(est$statistic, df = model$df.residual, lower.tail = FALSE)
  )
}
#Check original data
run_pathway("keep", "keep", "none")
```

### 4. Run all pathways
```{r}
# pmap() calls run_pathway() once for every row of multiverse_options,
# using the column names as argument names
results <- multiverse_options %>%
  mutate(output = pmap(multiverse_options, run_pathway)) %>%
  unnest(output) %>%
  mutate(
    significant = p_one < 0.05,
    pathway     = row_number()
  )

results
```

### 5. Summarise the multiverse
```{r}
# Summary statistics from the lecture: proportion of significant
# p-values, arithmetic mean and harmonic mean of the p-values
results %>%
  summarise(
    n_pathways        = n(),
    prop_significant  = mean(significant),
    mean_p            = mean(p_one),
    harmonic_mean_p   = n() / sum(1 / p_one),
    median_estimate   = median(estimate),
    min_estimate      = min(estimate),
    max_estimate      = max(estimate)
  )

# Proportion of significant pathways per option of each decision
results %>%
  pivot_longer(c(grade, comprehension, controls),
               names_to = "decision", values_to = "option") %>%
  group_by(decision, option) %>%
  summarise(prop_significant = mean(significant),
            mean_estimate = mean(estimate), .groups = "drop")
```

### 6. Importance of each decision (Sobol first-order effects)
```{r}
# For each decision, regress the estimates of all pathways on that
# decision alone. The R^2 is the proportion of variance in the
# estimates explained by that decision.
decisions <- c("grade", "comprehension", "controls")

sobol <- tibble(
  decision = decisions,
  r_squared = map_dbl(decisions, function(dec) {
    summary(lm(as.formula(paste("estimate ~", dec)), data = results))$r.squared
  })
)

sobol

ggplot(sobol, aes(x = reorder(decision, -r_squared), y = r_squared)) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey70", colour = "black") +
  labs(x = "Decision", y = "Proportion of variance explained") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### 7. Visualise the results
```{r}
# Specification curve: pathways sorted by their estimate, with the 95% CI.
# Filled points are significant (one-sided p < .05).
results_sorted <- results %>%
  arrange(estimate) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number(),
         is_partA = grade == "keep" & comprehension == "keep" & controls == "none")

spec_curve <- ggplot(results_sorted, aes(x = rank, y = estimate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = significant), size = 2) +
  geom_point(data = filter(results_sorted, is_partA),
             shape = 21, size = 4, stroke = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#1f5fbf", `FALSE` = "grey50"),
                      labels = c(`TRUE` = "p < .05", `FALSE` = "p >= .05")) +
  labs(x = "Pathway (sorted by estimate)",
       y = "Estimate of StatsCourses (b)",
       colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

# Lower panel: which option each pathway used
spec_panel <- results_sorted %>%
  pivot_longer(c(grade, comprehension, controls),
               names_to = "decision", values_to = "option") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = rank, y = option, colour = significant)) +
  geom_point(shape = 15, size = 1.5) +
  facet_grid(decision ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#1f5fbf", `FALSE` = "grey50"),
                      guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Pathway (sorted by estimate)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

spec_curve
spec_panel

# Histogram of the one-sided p-values
p_hist <- ggplot(results, aes(x = p_one)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.025, boundary = 0,
                 fill = "grey70", colour = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "One-sided p-value", y = "Number of pathways") +
  theme_minimal()

p_hist

```
